fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeMnNi alloy contains no aluminum, so the claimed reduction of aluminum depletion and formation of an alumina-based protective mechanism are chemically inconsistent with the stated material.
The intervention does not reconstruct the demonstrated low-temperature HVAF-i7 processing intervention or its optimized medium air/fuel setting.
No prior evidence is cited despite the request for supporting evidence.
The hierarchical columnar nanostructure is not operationally defined or linked to a feasible fabrication method.
The claimed 20–30% increase in thermal-cycling lifetime is unsupported by evidence or a quantitative model.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses HEA bond-coat durability at high temperature and proposes a comparative thermal-cycling experiment, but it diverges substantially from the target material, processing route, exposure range, and measured oxidation behavior. The target concerns dense FeCoNiCrAl deposited by optimized low-temperature HVAF-i7, yielding 0.2% porosity and a thin continuous alumina TGO during 50 h isothermal oxidation at 1000–1150 °C. In contrast, the generated proposal substitutes an unspecified nanostructured CoCrFeMnNi architecture and invokes aluminum depletion despite the stated alloy lacking Al. Its baseline, operating boundary, and falsification threshold are vague; the experiment has some discriminatory value because it includes a comparator and time-to-failure, but it lacks specified cycling parameters, sample size, statistical criterion, and oxide-composition measurements needed to test the proposed mechanism.
